hints: Write the equation as the continuous function $f(x)=x^3-3x-7$.
Evaluate $f(2)$ and $f(3)$ and use their opposite signs to bracket the stated unique real root.
walkthrough: Define the polynomial function $f(x) = x^3 - 3x - 7$, which is continuous on $\mathbb{R}$.

Since $f(x)$ is continuous on $[2, 3]$ and changes sign from negative at $x = 2$ to positive at $x = 3$, by the Intermediate Value Theorem there is at least one real root $\alpha$ in the interval $(2, 3)$. Since the equation has only one real root, $\alpha$ lies between 2 and 3.

ai_rubric.Numerical Root Bracketing: Endpoint evaluations at 2 and 3 establish the sign change or ordering. The final result is $2<\alpha<3$.

hints: Starting from $x_1=2.5$, calculate several terms from both formula A and formula B to compare their behaviour.
Identify failure to converge from terms that move away or oscillate with increasing size; use only the stable formula for the root.
List stable iterates to 4 decimal places, retaining full precision between steps, until they justify the same value to 2 decimal places.
walkthrough:
Test Formula $B$: $x_{n+1} = \dfrac{x_n^3 - 7}{3}$ starting with $x_1 = 2.5$:
$$x_2 = \dfrac{2.5^3 - 7}{3} = \dfrac{15.625 - 7}{3} = 2.8750$$
$$x_3 = \dfrac{2.8750^3 - 7}{3} \approx \dfrac{23.7637 - 7}{3} \approx 5.5879$$
$$x_4 = \dfrac{5.5879^3 - 7}{3} \approx \dfrac{174.479 - 7}{3} \approx 55.8264$$
The iterates grow rapidly without bound, showing that Formula $B$ fails to converge.

Verify that the root rounds to $2.43$ using the sign-change test on $f(x) = x^3 - 3x - 7$ across $[2.425, 2.435]$:
$$f(2.425) = (2.425)^3 - 3(2.425) - 7 \approx 14.2564 - 7.275 - 7 = -0.0186 < 0$$
$$f(2.435) = (2.435)^3 - 3(2.435) - 7 \approx 14.4329 - 7.305 - 7 = +0.1279 > 0$$
The sign change confirms that $\alpha = 2.43$ correct to 2 decimal places.

ai_rubric.Fixed-Point Iteration: Substitution into $\alpha$ gives consecutive iterates $2.43\to2.425\to2.435$, converging to Formula B fails to converge; formula A gives $\alpha=2.43$.
